findings.title: Use datetime-aware cursor conversion for audit logs
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key() applies math.floor()/math.ceil() directly to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so building cursors for any nonempty optimized response raises TypeError and returns a server error. value_from_cursor() also returns a raw number rather than converting it back to a datetime for subsequent queries. Inherit from DateTimePaginator or implement its datetime conversions before using this paginator for audit logs.

findings.title: Do not pass negative offsets to Django QuerySet slicing
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled and a cursor has a negative offset, this branch passes that offset directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django explicitly rejects negative slice indexes with ValueError; it does not handle them as the comment claims. Consequently, the advertised negative-offset pagination always fails with a server error rather than navigating backwards. Implement reverse navigation using supported ordering and nonnegative bounds, or reject these cursors with a pagination validation error.
